name: M-2 long bridge, probable Chenab River crossing
assumptions: River identity is inferred from position only: a dossier unknown. Satellite imagery confirms a wide braided river under the bridge, and travel writing says the M-2 crosses the Chenab, but no source names this exact bridge.
No ground-level or side photograph of this bridge was found. Only overhead imagery (Esri, Bing) was inspected, so everything below the deck is inferred.
Spans of 52 m and piers at each joint group are read from Esri joints and Bing shadow bumps; no source publishes the span count. The pier positions at joint-group centres are a guess.

Deck level 194 m is an estimate: Terrarium shows approaches at 192 to 194 m and a 7 m shadow implies about 12 m of clearance over the 182 to 186 m bed, at an assumed sun elevation of about 60 degrees.
Deck is taken level with no vertical curve or crossfall; none could be measured.

Superstructure is the plainest single-cell box girder 3 m deep; one Structurae entry describes a girder bridge at Bhaira completed 1997 and built by incremental launching, but its river is unstated, and the section here is not from a source.
Pier form is the plainest option: one round-ended solid wall per deck under a rectangular cap, founded below the bed. No pile caps, footings or river training works are modelled.
Abutment placement at the first and last joint group centres is a guess.
South deck outer strip about 5.5 m wide is read from both overhead photos; it may be partly the sunlit south face of the deck.
Lateral bands were shifted 1.5 m so carriageway A sits on the OSM line used by the game; imagery and OSM differ by that much here.
Parapet shape and heights (1.0 m outer, 0.9 m inner) are estimates; the parapets appear only as pale lines overhead.
All below-deck colours are estimates; surface colours are sampled from overhead imagery with atmospheric tint reduced.
West approach embankment and its side slopes are simple estimates; the terrain model in the game replaces the real ground.
Alignment is the straight OSM chord; the OSM points stay within about 3 m of it.
suppress is empty on purpose: the dossier footprint is a road centreline over a river, and flattening the ground under it would cut the river bed.
No night lighting: no source describes any.
